accuracy.reason: All five objectives accurately distinguish roles, HTTP syntax from payload meaning, local session state from stateless handlers, service benefits/dependencies and uncertain no-response outcomes. Live RFC and platform guidance support the claims.

evidence.quote: These are roles in an interaction, not types of computer.

mechanisms.reason: Request interpretation/access checks/work/response is traceable. Local-memory dependency explains server-switch failure; shared storage explains replaceable handlers while preserving a dependency. Network loss explains why missing responses do not prove missing work.

evidence.quote: No response leaves the outcome uncertain: processing may have failed, or processing may have succeeded and only the response was lost.

coherence.reason: Roles precede protocol, session placement, tradeoffs and complete interaction. Each card objective and its prerequisites are covered; inspected diagrams align request arrows, optional database, session variants and client/server tradeoffs with prose.

evidence.quote: Locate persistent application data and any session context separately.

decisions.reason: The lesson supports where to run work, keeping trusted checks at the resource service, choosing shared versus local context, and recognizing finite capacity/retry uncertainty. Benefits and costs are both causal.

evidence.quote: Overload can increase waiting or require rejection; the client/server model alone guarantees neither capacity nor availability.

clarity.reason: Plain definitions explain role, protocol and session state, with familiar sign-in context and clear diagrams. API/payload terminology is sufficient for programmers; one specific full interaction could improve transfer, but the learner constructs a supported generic flow. UI source inspected, not executed.

evidence.quote: Session state is context retained across related requests, such as sign-in status.

outcomes.reason: Learner covers role definitions and dual-role/same-machine possibilities, protocol agreement, all request/response components and independent application meanings/errors.

Learner covers local session dependence, server replacement/routing loss, supplied/shared request context, persistent data and auth in stateless handlers, shared-rule benefits and network/capacity/availability costs.

Learner constructs a supported shared-data flow, locates persistent data and session context, traces permission checks and outcomes, and distinguishes reported errors from uncertain missing responses.

sourceChecks.claim: Live inspected RFC 9110 section 3.3: client/server are connection roles, and one program can perform both. Roles do not specify machine class.

Live inspected RFC 9110 sections 1.3 and 3.4: request method/target/headers/content and response status/headers/content; interpretation and application error meanings remain required. Server access checks align with RFC authorization semantics.

Live inspected Azure autoscaling design guidance: avoid instance affinity assumptions and design stateless services. Local process memory versus retrievable/shared context explains the lesson replacement and routing consequences.

Live inspected MDN server-side introduction: shared data, access control and server responsibilities. RFC overload responses and Azure scaling guidance support finite capacity and network/dependency costs; client-side hiding cannot enforce server authorization.

Live inspected RFC 9110 section 9.2.2: communications failure before response can follow executed work, so retry safety depends on semantics. Reported errors and absent responses provide different evidence.
